exactGap: Filesystem confinement is real and fails closed (bubblewrap read-only root, cleared environment, pid, uts and ipc unshare, unsandboxed spawn refused for ReadOnly and WorkspaceWrite), the container runs a scoped seccomp deny-list profile (deploy/seccomp-bwrap.json), the production overlay drops all capabilities, and both code_interpreter and the background process host hard-code MpNetworkPolicy::Disabled (--unshare-net), so no Space agent code path has network today; AllowDomains is checked only by the presence of HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY and no proxy is configured in the Model Plane compose files. Missing: CPU, memory and pid caps or rlimits (only a wall-clock timeout and a 64 KiB output cap exist, sandbox-manager limits count live processes and output bytes, and the Model Plane deploy compose files set no memory, cpu or pid limits), a network-namespace-with-proxy design for AllowDomains, any per-room egress allowlist (Control's Space capability decision has only a coarse space:egress permission), and a lease is mandatory only for Space-scoped code_interpreter (fails closed through ensure_sandbox_lease), not for every Space agent. The SSRF part is already the architecture: Quarry owns dns_guard, a deny-by-default DNS-pinned browser egress proxy and redirect re-validation, and the gateway forwards URLs instead of dialing them (public_url.rs with the ssrf_forward_not_fetch test), with a documented decision against a shared crate.

constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes: agent web access should keep going through Quarry (egress proxy, receipts) rather than giving the sandbox a general network. approachAdjustment: Split the item: (1) per-spawn resource caps (prlimit or rlimit in the spawn wrapper, or container-level cgroup limits in compose), the only gap that bites today; (2) defer AllowDomains netns plus proxy and per-room egress until a feature actually needs sandbox network, because the default is already no network and Quarry is the sanctioned path; (3) replace 'one shared SSRF-safe connector crate' with 'any new unfurl or webhook goes through a Quarry endpoint and the gateway forward-don't-fetch test' (no link unfurl exists in the gateway today); (4) extend the existing Control space:egress decision before inventing effective_egress.
effortNote: L to M for what is worth doing now (resource caps, one cross-plane lease rule). The netns-with-proxy and audience-intersection egress remain L and should be deferred behind a concrete need.
verdictReason: Partly misdescribes current state: network is already off by default for every Space code path, a container seccomp profile and production hardening exist, the lease is already required for Space code_interpreter, and the SSRF boundary is already Quarry with a documented decision against a shared crate. The genuinely open gap is resource caps.

exactGap: Every Space post is a model turn: SpaceRoomComposer.submitMessage always calls streamChat and the gateway Space router has no POST route for threads or messages. A non-owner reply is refused twice in Session Core, because AppendMessage runs authorize_thread_owner(Mutate) (grpc.rs:4495-4506, auth.rs:492-530) and verify_append_space_decision compares the signed decision subject with the thread OWNER (grpc.rs:2498), although Control already issues a member-capable thread:append decision (editor/manager/owner) and messages already store author_subject_id (migration 0035). No thread panel, reply counters or agent-stake record exist, ?thread_id= links from activity-grammar.ts are never consumed (SpaceCockpit reads only the hash), and the third column (SpacePulse) is a read-only status rail.
reuse: Gateway inject_personal_thread_context (spaces.rs:49-184) already mints the Control thread:append decision from a bare space_ref and thread_id; a no-invoke POST route can call the same helper.
Control IssueThreadAppendDecision / ValidateForSharedThread (personal_thread_decision.go) is already member-capable for editor, manager and owner, so no new space:post decision type is required.
Session Core append_message_in_tx already stamps the audience columns and author_subject_id on each message and writes the MESSAGE_APPENDED event atomically.
Room-level read marker (convex spaceReadMarkers.ts) plus the browser mirror space-unread.ts already derive unread thread ids, so per-thread unread does not need to wait for a new projection.

constraints: Session Core owns transcript truth, so every human post must go through AppendMessage with a Control-signed, content-digest-bound thread:append decision (viewers cannot obtain one). Space access must not widen an owner-plane ACL: relaxing the owner check must apply only to Space-bound threads and must verify that the decision subject equals the authenticated caller, never the thread owner. A non-owner append currently also rewrites the thread-level audience columns (grpc.rs:2499-2515); that UPDATE must not move earlier members' history to a newer revision. The agent turn must run with the invoker's grants (model-gateway appends carry the caller's bearer). Session Core already refuses durable writes from ZDR credentials (auth.rs:276-285), so human posts are never stored for ZDR callers.
approachAdjustment: Do not add a new Control space:post decision type; reuse thread:append (already minted at spaces.rs:49-184). The Session Core change has two parts, not one: drop authorize_thread_owner for Space-bound threads in favour of 'caller is the decision subject and the decision verifies', and change verify_append_space_decision to compare claims.subject_id with the caller (author) instead of the thread owner; also make the append stamp the new message instead of rewriting the thread-level audience columns for everyone. The R-t1-12-01 slice (AuxPane, ?thread_id= consumption, explicit 'you cannot read these turns' state using the existing transcript route) can ship Frontend-only first. Reply counters can be derived at read time until volume demands a thread_metadata table, and per-thread unread can reuse the existing room marker rather than wait for S1.7.
effortNote: Unchanged for the whole item, but it is really two slices: M for the frontend and gateway thread panel and deep link, L for Session Core plus Control plus the no-invoke append and mention-gated agent turn.
verdictReason: Accurately described and verified in code: the composer always streams a model turn and non-owner replies cannot succeed, so the item is not already built. Adjust the approach as above (reuse thread:append, fix the decision-subject check, do not rewrite thread audience on append).

exactGap: Audience binding is real for thread and message storage and transcript reads (Control-signed decisions bind audience ref, hash and revision, messages carry audience columns, reads drop rows newer than the decision revision, revoked members are denied), but memory is not Space-aware at all. In Session Core, append_message_in_tx extracts memory candidates from every message that is not conversation-only, including Space posts, and persists them as user-level agent_memory owned by the thread owner (dreaming.rs persist_candidates) and mirrors them to Letta, while search_memory authorizes only against the thread owner and filters by org, user and thread; agent_memory has no space, audience or label column. There are also no per-entry source labels on tool results or compaction summaries, no declassify or personal-context opt-in, no private draft, no audience-intersected retrieval entitlement (Control's shared retrieval decision binds the audience but evaluates the acting member, and Data v2 retrieval-engine has no audience concept) and no Space-binding knowledge scope (knowledge_scope is deliberately not stored; only per-agent-definition knowledgeBindings exist).

Space access must not widen an owner-plane ACL: user or org-scope memory read inside a Space needs an owner-signed Control decision, and room facts must never be auto-copied into personal memory. ZDR callers already get no durable memory. Letta must receive the same filter or it becomes the bypass.
approachAdjustment: Add a small containment slice before the full labelling design: for Space-bound threads, stop extracting memory candidates into user-level agent_memory and stop Letta indexing (at minimum for non-personal Spaces), and exclude user and org-scope memory recall from shared-room turns until a Control opt-in exists; then tag agent_memory rows with space_ref, audience hash and revision and filter at retrieval. Treat source-scope labels, compaction taint, declassify, private drafts and per-room knowledge lists as the later L phase. Audience-intersection of retrieval entitlement belongs in the Control decision (which today evaluates one acting member), not in Data v2 inferring membership.
effortNote: Unchanged for the full item. The containment slice is M; the labelling and declassify phase spans Session Core, Control, Data v2 and the Letta bridge and is L to XL.
verdictReason: Premise confirmed and sharper than described: a Space message is already turned into the thread owner's user-level memory with no Space tag, so the leak vector exists today. Keep, add the containment slice, and consider raising priority.

exactGap: Session Core already enforces ZDR on the caller's verified token claim (authorize_operation refuses every non-read scope on CreateThread, AppendMessage and StartRun, MemoryRetention plus authorize_memory_preflight gate durable and Letta memory, run output is refused and a ZDR managed start is metadata-only); only the Space decision's own zero_data_retention flag is still decoded and discarded (grpc.rs:1749-1755), which Control and the gateway make unreachable today. Execution-core, letta-bridge, notification-core, Quarry and Control also refuse, and a typed refusal catalogue (mp-contracts zdr_refusal.rs, api/contracts/zdr-refusals.json), a posture-matrix golden and the SPA presentation module zdr-refusals.ts (wired into the Space composer through translateApiError) exist, but the catalogue, retention receipts, matrix test and SPA module are still untracked in git. Real remaining gaps: Session Core's own refusals are plain strings rather than typed codes, per-Space ZDR is explicitly 'not applied in v1' (matrix policy.space_zdr, honest-limits L14), sandbox-manager has no ZDR flag (covered only by execution-core's upstream refusal), the README-referenced scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh is missing, and no content-free telemetry label guard was found.

constraints: ZDR must propagate and a missing claim must fail closed (already the case). A Space is a durable shared transcript by design, so Session Core already refuses Space thread creation and appends for ZDR callers; the product decision is how that is worded, not whether to enforce it. approachAdjustment: Replace 'Session Core must act on the decision flag' with a small hardening list: (1) commit the untracked catalogue, retention receipt, matrix test and SPA module; (2) return the typed durable-mutation refusal from authorize_operation and memory_grpc preflight instead of plain strings; (3) cross-check the decision's zero_data_retention against caller.zdr() in the Space decision verifiers so a ZDR-flagged decision can never persist; (4) record the Space-ZDR product decision (L14) and add a sandbox-manager flag only if leases ever become reachable by ZDR callers; (5) restore or drop the README's zdr-contract-sync script and add a label allowlist check for Prometheus and error reports.
effortNote: M to S: the enforcement matrix, typed catalogue and cross-plane refusals are built; what is left is committing work in progress, typing two refusal sites, one cross-check and a product note. Applying per-Space ZDR would be a separate M or L item.
verdictReason: Largely exists in the code, and the item's central premise (Session Core ignores ZDR and must be made to refuse durable thread, message and memory writes) misdescribes the state. Keep only the residual hardening above and move it out of the W1 priority slot.
